memory_update.text: AXTI should be promoted to the next verification layer as the closest US-listed direct compound-substrate candidate for InP/GaAs/Ge exposure tied to optical communications and data-center connectivity.
MTRN remains a plausible but weakly proven precision-materials candidate; survival depends on finding direct optical-transceiver, silicon-photonics, laser, or CPO customer evidence.
COHR defines the reference stack: InP wafers, lasers, modulators, photodiodes, 1.6T transceiver components, and CPO laser sources. Smaller candidates should be tested against this stack.
The biggest evidence gap is not whether AI optical demand exists, but whether independent small/mid-cap material suppliers have qualified supply positions at 800G/1.6T transceiver or CPO customers.

node: Compound substrates and precision materials for 800G/1.6T optical transceivers and co-packaged optics
summary: Layer 1B expands the US-listed universe around the hidden materials and photonics-input layer beneath AI optical networking. The strongest direct underfollowed candidate is AXTI because public filings describe InP, GaAs and Ge substrate wafers used for data-center connectivity. COHR is included as the reference anchor because it has disclosed InP technology, 1.6T transceiver-enabling products, and CPO laser products, but it is not underfollowed. MTRN is a weaker but plausible precision-materials candidate that needs verification of direct optical-transceiver or photonics revenue exposure. POET is a speculative-shadow candidate: not a substrate supplier, but its optical-interposer/optical-engine position may expose it to the same 800G/1.6T qualification gates and laser-material dependencies.
